User Story: As a Customer Support Specialist (CSS), I want a single intake screen for all products, so that I can create quotes without navigating multiple modules.
Description: Day 3 introduced replacing fragmented QuickBase flows with a unified orchestration screen. The intake must centralize customer, site, product, pricing, and scheduling into one structured workflow. This reduces context switching and speeds up live calls.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Intake screen must allow product selection first.
2. Customer lookup embedded within intake.
3. Site selection or creation inline.
4. Pricing visible without page navigation.
5. Saving creates related records in one workflow.
Notes: Architectural backbone of Cube replacing multi-tab quoting.

Task Name: Render Fields Based on Product Selection
User Story: As a Customer Support Specialist (CSS), I want intake fields to dynamically change based on product type, so that I only see relevant inputs.
Description: Product-first design was emphasized. Each ZTERS product line has unique required fields. The UI must adapt automatically.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Product selection triggers dynamic field rendering.
2. Irrelevant fields hidden.
3. Required fields update dynamically.
4. Switching product clears incompatible inputs.
5. Rendering under 1 second.
Notes: Prevents clutter and user confusion across 9 product lines.

User Story: As a Customer Support Specialist (CSS), I want to search and select customers within intake, so that I avoid leaving the quote flow.
Description: Customer lookup must be embedded to prevent workflow interruption during live calls.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Search by name, phone, or email.
2. Results appear in under 1 second.
3. Select customer without leaving intake.
4. Option to create new if not found.
5. Preserve intake state during lookup.

User Story: As a Customer Support Specialist (CSS), I want to create a site inline, so that quoting does not require separate navigation.
Description: Site creation must occur within the unified intake modal.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Site form opens in modal.
2. Address validation required.
3. Save attaches site to intake record.
4. Prevent duplicate sites by address.
5. Closing modal preserves intake progress.

User Story: As a Customer Support Specialist (CSS), I want pricing calculated within intake, so that margin visibility is immediate.
Description: Pricing engine from Day 2 must be embedded directly into intake.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Vendor cost editable inline.
2. Suggested rate auto-calculated.
3. Real-time margin display.
4. Approval triggers visible instantly.
5. Block save below hard floor margin.

User Story: As a Customer Support Specialist (CSS), I want all related records created in one transaction, so that partial data is never saved.
Description: Intake must prevent orphan records when failures occur.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Save creates Customer, Site, Quote together.
2. Rollback entire transaction if any failure.
3. Clear error messaging.
4. Log failure details.
5. Prevent duplicate submission.

User Story: As a Customer Support Specialist (CSS), I want to see account summary during intake, so that I understand financial risk while quoting.
Description: Context panel prevents quoting blind to account issues.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Show outstanding balance.
2. Show active products.
3. Show recent tickets.
4. Refresh when customer changes.
5. Load under 2 seconds.
Notes: Reduces risk of quoting delinquent accounts.

User Story: As a Customer Support Specialist (CSS), I want clear draft and finalized states, so that workflow is controlled.
Description: Quote lifecycle must be clearly defined.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Draft editable.
2. Finalized locked.
3. Pending Approval visible.
4. Status indicator prominent.
5. Log state transitions.

User Story: As a Customer Support Specialist (CSS), I want an embedded map during intake, so that I confirm service location visually.
Description: Visual confirmation reduces mis-delivery.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Display map based on address.
2. Show geocoded coordinates.
3. Allow correction.
4. Save coordinates to site.
5. Handle invalid address.

User Story: As a Customer Support Specialist (CSS), I want fulfillment optionally created when quote finalizes, so that operations are triggered immediately.
Description: Reduces delay between sale and execution.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Toggle to create fulfillment.
2. Only after approval if required.
3. Link fulfillment to quote ID.
4. Notify operations.
5. Prevent duplicates.

User Story: As a Customer Support Specialist (CSS), I want duplicate quotes detected, so that customers are not double-billed.
Description: Duplicate prevention protects revenue integrity.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Detect same customer + site + product within time window.
2. Show warning.
3. Allow override with justification.
4. Log override.
5. Block accidental double submit.

User Story: As a Customer Support Specialist (CSS), I want keyboard shortcuts, so that intake speed improves during live calls.
Description: Call efficiency matters at scale.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Logical tab order.
2. Enter submits draft.
3. Shortcut for search.
4. Shortcut for save.
5. No forced mouse-only actions.

User Story: As a Customer Support Specialist (CSS), I want to adjust pricing before finalization, so that negotiations can occur without restarting.
Description: Draft flexibility supports real-world sales.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Unlimited edits in draft state.
2. Recalculate margin instantly.
3. Maintain edit history.
4. Trigger approval if needed.
5. Preserve audit trail.

User Story: As a Customer Support Specialist (CSS), I want to schedule delivery during intake, so that operations alignment happens immediately.
Description: Scheduling must not require separate navigation.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Select date inline.
2. Validate blackout dates.
3. Sync with operations calendar.
4. Prevent past dates.
5. Save to fulfillment record.

User Story: As a Customer Success Manager (CSM), I want intake duration measured, so that quoting efficiency is monitored.
Description: Performance metrics matter for scaling teams.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Record start timestamp.
2. Record completion timestamp.
3. Calculate duration automatically.
4. Exclude abandoned drafts.
5. Include in dashboard report.

User Story: As an Administrator (Admin), I want intake access restricted by role, so that unauthorized users cannot create quotes.
Description: Access control protects pricing authority.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Only CSS and CSM allowed.
2. Block direct URL access.
3. Log access attempts.
4. Configurable permission matrix.
5. Clear access denied message.

User Story: As a Customer Support Specialist (CSS), I want intake drafts auto-saved, so that data is not lost during long calls.
Description: Autosave prevents frustration and data loss.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Save every 60 seconds.
2. Restore on reload.
3. Notify user of autosave.
4. Prevent duplicate drafts.
5. Allow manual save override.

User Story: As a Customer Support Specialist (CSS), I want validation errors shown inline, so that I correct issues immediately.
Description: Clear validation improves speed and accuracy.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Highlight missing required fields.
2. Provide descriptive messages.
3. Prevent save until resolved.
4. Preserve entered data.
5. Scroll to first error.

User Story: As a Customer Support Specialist (CSS), I want to cancel intake drafts safely, so that incomplete records do not clutter the system.
Description: Draft cancellation must not delete linked records accidentally.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Confirmation prompt required.
2. Delete draft only.
3. Preserve audit entry.
4. Do not delete customer record.
5. Return to dashboard.

User Story: As a Customer Success Manager (CSM), I want to track conversion rate from intake to fulfillment, so that sales effectiveness is measurable.
Description: Conversion analytics help evaluate intake quality.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Track finalized quotes.
2. Track fulfillment creation.
3. Calculate conversion percentage.
4. Filter by user and region.
5. Exportable report.
